neighbours.label: Period after the year in a parenthetical author-year citation ('(Smith, J. 2014.'), vs periods in ordinary sentences that end with a year
fire:
Most clinics reported shortages.
(Martin, L. 2011. Supply chains in rural care. Lyon.)

The survey covered nine villages.
(Okafor, B. 2016. Water access in the Delta. Lagos.)

Prices doubled within a year.
(Keller, P. 2009. Grain markets after reform. Bern.)

Literacy rose steadily after 1950.
(Haddad, R. 2013. Schools and the state. Beirut.)

Few farms used fertilizer.
(Lindgren, A. 2005. Soil and harvest. Uppsala.)

The fishing fleet shrank by half.
(Moreau, C. 2018. Coastal economies. Brest.)

Migration to cities accelerated.
(Tanaka, H. 2012. Urban growth in Asia. Kyoto.)

The rail line closed in winter.
(Novak, J. 2007. Transport and isolation. Brno.)
quiet: Most clinics reported shortages. The first new clinic opened in 2011. More followed.
The survey covered nine villages. It was completed in 2016. Results came later.
Prices doubled within a year. The reform began in 2009. Farmers protested.
Literacy rose steadily. Most schools were built by 2013. Many are still open.
Few farms used fertilizer. That changed around 2005. Yields then improved.
The fishing fleet shrank by half. The last cannery closed in 2018. Jobs vanished.
Migration to cities accelerated. The census was held in 2012. It counted millions.
The rail line closed in winter. It reopened in 2007. Service is now daily.

predictions: Citation periods reach 0.3-0.7; sentence-final periods after a year stay under 0.1.
